patch_description:
Building on the strongest prior ansatz (the orbit-shared RY decoder + CRY line-segment entangler that scored 0.53), I introduce a richer but still parameter-efficient and symmetry-aware entangling scheme.

Key insights:
1. The fixed measurements group corners→circle, edges→cross, center→draw. Winning lines couple a corner, an edge, and either the center or another corner. So the decisive correlations are *corner↔edge* and *edge↔center*. The prior ansatz only routed corner→edge (CRY [corner,edge]) one direction. I add the reverse edge→corner direction with its own shared parameter, giving the circuit bidirectional information flow along every grid edge — this directly implements the recommended "diagonal two-cell correlation" motif using the corner↔edge adjacency.
2. I add a layer of RZ rotations *between* the entanglers. After CRY gates rotate amplitude out of the Y-quadrature into accessible directions, a trainable RZ can re-phase and (combined with the surrounding RY) build genuinely 3-axis local frames, increasing expressivity per qubit at the cost of only 3 shared parameters (corner/edge/center orbits).
3. Center↔edge bidirectional CRY (already present one way) is kept and balanced so the draw readout (z[8]) gets line context and broadcasts back.
4. All gates are shared by D4 board orbit (corner/edge/center), keeping the per-block parameter count low (12 unique params → 72 total, same budget as the best prior) while increasing the effective entangling structure and the local rotation rank. This preserves the small train-test gap while raising accuracy.

The block structure per upload-repeat is:
RY decode → CRY corner→edge → CRY edge→corner → CRY edge→center → CRY center→edge → mid RZ orbit phases → RY readout → RX readout.
